articles.title: Aram and Israel: A Shared Heritage
articles.summary: Arameans and the Hebrew Patriarchs have shared origins and marriage ties existed between the peoples.

articles.title: The Kaldu-Arameans in southern Babylonia
articles.summary: The Chaldeans (Kaldu) were West Semitic Aramean tribes who settled in southern Babylonia and ultimately conquered and destroyed the Assyrian Empire.

articles.title: A Scribal Error in the Chronicle of Michael the Great
articles.summary: A missing word and comma in a copied manuscript of the Chronicle of Michael the Great altered the meaning of a key passage on Aramean identity.

articles.title: The Aramaic of Tur Abdin: Urhay, Suryaya, and Turoyo
articles.summary: Tur Abdin preserves a living Aramaic heritage linking the Edessan literary tradition with the spoken Turoyo/Surayt variety.

articles.title: Israel recognizes the Arameans as separate nationality
articles.summary: The State of Israel recognizes the Arameans as separate nationality in Israel.

articles.title: The Aramean Genocide (Sayfo)
articles.summary: Seyfo was the mass killing, deportation, and destruction of Aramean communities under Ottoman rule during World War I, especially from 1915 to 1918.

articles.title: Max von Oppenheim and Tell Halaf
articles.summary: Max von Oppenheim’s excavations at Tell Halaf revealed Guzana, an important Aramean center in ancient northern Mesopotamia.

articles.title: Arameans of Bet Urhay (Osroene): The First Nation to Accept Christianity
articles.summary: Jesus sent his disciple Thaddeus (Addai) to Bet Urhay to proclaim the Gospel and to heal their king.

articles.title: The Simele Massacre (1933)
articles.summary: The Simele Massacre was a campaign of mass killings, displacement, and destruction against Aramean communities in northern Iraq in August 1933.

articles.title: The Abgar Dynasty: Aramean Kings of Edessa
articles.summary: The Abgarid dynasty ruled the Aramean kingdom of Osroene from Edessa, linking Aramean political life to Roman-Parthian history and later Christian tradition.
